action: WatchGuard advises treating installers from third-party download portals as untrusted, checking Defender's exclusion list and Controlled Folder Access on affected endpoints, and hunting for legitimate executables running from C:\Users\Public\Documents.
date_note: WatchGuard's post, published 25 November, describes activity from mid-September 2026; the post gives no earlier disclosure day.

evidence.quote: a Windows executable of about 114 MB (113,685,436 bytes)

exec: WatchGuard reports a fake oCam installer that installs the real app while loading a Gh0stRAT variant, so users may not notice an infection.

sources.name: WatchGuard: Silver Fox SEO poisoning, how fake software downloads spread
Cyber Press: Hackers hide spyware in fake software downloads

summary: WatchGuard researchers say a fake installer for the Windows screen recorder oCam, downloaded from a third-party portal in mid-September 2026, installed the genuine app and a Gh0stRAT variant. The download was a Windows executable of about 114 MB, and a PowerShell step tried to add broad Microsoft Defender exclusions. WatchGuard attributes the campaign to Silver Fox, calling its evidence consistent with that profile.
title: WatchGuard: fake oCam installer delivers Gh0stRAT, attributed to Silver Fox

validation.note: WatchGuard is the only research source; Cyber Press relays it and is not independent.

plain: WatchGuard says a fake installer for the oCam screen recorder installed the real app plus a Gh0stRAT remote-access variant. It attributes the campaign to Silver Fox.
